mainTopic: Tearing up a heavenly גזר דין: individual versus community, the ten days of תשובה, judgment on ראש השנה, and the months when messengers go out
overview: The גמרא explains that the rule 'no forgiveness after the גזר דין' applies only to a יחיד, while a ציבור can be forgiven even after its sentence. It then shows that the individual's case is a disagreement. רבי מאיר says a complete prayer decides, רבי אלעזר says prayer helps only before the sentence, and רבי יצחק says crying out helps both before and after. Next the גמרא asks whether even a community's decree can be torn up. It answers that only a decree sealed with a שבועה cannot be undone, as with ה׳'s oath against בית עלי. רבא and אביי say that תורה, and also גמילות חסדים, can still atone for that family, and stories about רבה, אביי and a family in ירושלים show it. רב teaches that a community's sealed decree can still be torn up. An individual, though, has a special time to reach ה׳: the ten days from ראש השנה to יום הכפורים. The גמרא then explains the משנה's phrase 'כבני מרון' and teaches that ה׳ sees everyone in one look. Finally a new משנה lists the months when messengers announce ראש חודש, and the גמרא asks why תמוז and טבת are not included.

steps.title: The verse resolution seems to say no forgiveness after the sentence
steps.stepSummary: The earlier answer, that one פסוק speaks of before the גזר דין and the other of after it, implies that after the sentence there is no forgiveness. That clashes with רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is before the sentence, and there it is after the sentence!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of an earlier teaching that the גמרא is using against רבי יוחנן. That teaching settled two clashing פסוקים by saying one is before the גזר דין and one is after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer split the פסוקים: forgiveness before the גזר דין, no forgiveness after it. But רבי יוחנן said תשובה tears up a person's גזר דין, which means forgiveness even after it. So the answer itself creates a new problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The heavenly sentence or verdict passed on a person

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new idea. It repeats the earlier answer, and the exclamation mark shows it is now being used as a challenge.

phrases.english: Here, it is before the sentence;
there, it is after the sentence!

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּאן קוֹדֶם גְּזַר דִּין, כָּאן לְאַחַר גְּזַר דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the previous section, where the before/after answer was given.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that תשובה tears up a person's גזר דין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If forgiveness only works before the sentence, then after the sentence תשובה would not help, which contradicts רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Here too it refers to an individual
steps.stepSummary: The 'no forgiveness after the sentence' rule applies only to a יחיד. A ציבור can be forgiven even after the sentence.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is speaking about an individual.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the limit only applies to a single person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא used the difference between a יחיד and a ציבור to protect רבי יוחנן. The words 'here too' reuse that same answer. For a community, תשובה works even after the גזר דין, so רבי יוחנן's teaching still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, the same answer applies
An individual, as opposed to a ציבור (community)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question: what exactly happens to an individual after his sentence? The גמרא will show that this is a disagreement.

phrases.english: Here too, it refers to an individual.
phrases.notes: 'Too' points back to the earlier answer that split between a single person and a community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to an individual (יחיד) as opposed to a community (ציבור)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After the sentence, no one can be forgiven, which contradicts רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an individual loses that chance after the sentence. A community can still be forgiven.

steps.title: An individual's sentence is a disagreement: רבי מאיר's two cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the status of an individual's sentence is debated by תנאים. It brings רבי מאיר's ברייתא about two people in identical danger who end up differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sentence of an individual is a dispute between תנאים. As it is taught: רבי מאיר used to say: two people take to bed with the same illness, or two people go up to the court to be judged with the same sentence. One comes down from his bed and the other does not. One is saved and the other is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section. It says the individual's sentence is a disagreement and begins quoting רבי מאיר's teaching. The explanation comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two people are described as equal in every way: same illness, same sentence. Yet one survives and the other does not. This sets up the puzzle of what made the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a disagreement between תנאים
The court or platform where a person is judged

phrases.english: And the sentence of an individual is a dispute of תנאים.
As it is taught: רבי מאיר used to say:
Two who went up to bed, and their illness is the same,
phrases.notes: 'Went up to bed' means they became sick and were bedridden.

phrases.english: and likewise two who went up to the court to be judged
and their sentence is the same.
This one came down and that one did not come down,
phrases.notes: He came down from his sickbed, meaning he recovered.

phrases.english: this one was saved and that one was not saved.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּגְזַר דִּין דְּיָחִיד תַּנָּאֵי הִיא. דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 2's focus on the individual and shows that his case is debated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people in equal danger can have different outcomes. The reason is explained next.

steps.title: Why did one survive and the other not?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what caused the different outcomes for two people in the same situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what reason did this one come down and that one not come down, this one was saved and that one was not saved?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר asks the obvious question about his own cases, preparing for his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the illness and the sentence were identical, the difference must come from something the people themselves did.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה זֶה יָרַד וְזֶה לֹא יָרַד,
phrases.english: For what reason did this one come down and that one not come down,
this one was saved and that one was not saved?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה זֶה יָרַד וְזֶה לֹא יָרַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the cases described in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What made the difference between two people in identical situations?

steps.title: One prayed and was answered, the other was not
steps.stepSummary: Both prayed, but only one was answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one prayed and was answered, and that one prayed and was not answered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives a first answer: the difference was in how their prayers were received.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'one prayed and one didn't' would have been simple. Instead both prayed, so the answer only moves the question one step back: why was one prayer accepted?

phrases.english: This one prayed and was answered,
and that one prayed and was not answered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both prayed. One prayer was answered and the other was not.

steps.title: Why was one prayer answered and not the other?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what made one prayer succeed.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what reason was this one answered and that one not answered?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר pushes the question deeper, setting up his real point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both people prayed, the difference must be in the quality of the prayer itself.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה זֶה נַעֲנָה וְזֶה לֹא נַעֲנָה?
phrases.english: For what reason was this one answered and that one not answered?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה זֶה נַעֲנָה וְזֶה לֹא נַעֲנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What made one prayer accepted and the other not?

steps.title: A complete prayer is answered
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר concludes that the one who prayed a complete prayer was answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one prayed a complete prayer and was answered. That one did not pray a complete prayer and was not answered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives his final answer: the difference was a full, wholehearted prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי מאיר's view, timing is not the deciding factor. The quality of the prayer is. Since the two people had the same sentence, his view suggests that a complete prayer can save an individual even when a sentence exists.

keyTerms.meaning: A complete prayer, prayed with the whole heart

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the outcome depends on whether the person prayed a תפלה שלימה, a complete, wholehearted prayer.

phrases.english: This one prayed a complete prayer and was answered,
phrases.notes: 'Complete' here means with his whole heart, not just saying every word.

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה לֹא הִתְפַּלֵּל תְּפִלָּה שְׁלֵימָה — לֹא נַעֲנָה
phrases.english: and that one did not pray a complete prayer and was not answered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 and completes רבי מאיר's teaching.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The quality of the prayer, whether it was a complete prayer, decides whether it is answered.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: it depends on before or after the sentence
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains the difference by timing. One prayed before the גזר דין and the other prayed after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: here it was before the sentence, and there it was after the sentence.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a different explanation for the two people's different outcomes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, the deciding factor is timing, not the quality of the prayer. The person who prayed after his sentence was issued was not answered. So in his view, an individual's sentence cannot be torn up once it is issued.
steps.confusionAlert: These words sound exactly like step 1, but here they are רבי אלעזר's explanation of the two people in רבי מאיר's teaching.

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said:
Here, it was before the sentence;
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the one who was answered. He prayed before his sentence was decided.

phrases.english: there, it was after the sentence.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: כָּאן קוֹדֶם גְּזַר דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation from רבי מאיר's of the same cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prayer helps an individual only before the גזר דין, not after.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: crying out helps both before and after the sentence
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק holds that crying out to ה׳ helps a person whether before or after the גזר דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: crying out is good for a person both before the sentence and after the sentence.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק disagrees with רבי אלעזר and says the timing does not stop prayer from working.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק says a person's cry to ה׳ is effective even after the sentence has been issued. So in his view, even an individual's גזר דין can be torn up, against רבי אלעזר. The disagreement is now fully laid out.

keyTerms.meaning: Crying out in prayer to ה׳

steps.whatToRemember: The three views on an individual's sentence: רבי מאיר says a complete prayer decides. רבי אלעזר says prayer helps only before the גזר דין. רבי יצחק says crying out helps both before and after it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the rule 'no help after the sentence for an individual' (step 2) is not agreed by everyone. רבי יצחק holds that even an individual can be helped after the sentence.

phrases.english: רבי יצחק said:
Crying out is good for a person
both before the sentence
and after the sentence.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר: יָפָה צְעָקָה לָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אלעזר in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crying out to ה׳ is effective for an individual both before and after the גזר דין.

steps.title: Can a community's sealed decree really be torn up?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether a גזר דין on a ציבור can be canceled, citing two contradictory פסוקים that suggest repentance does not help after the decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can a decree on a community really be torn up? One פסוק says, 'Wash your heart from wickedness,' which means washing helps. Another פסוק says, 'Even if you wash with lye and much soap, your sin stays as a stain before Me,' which means washing does not help. Isn't the answer that the first is before the גזר דין and the second is after it? If so, after the decree nothing helps, even for a community!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that a decree on a community can be canceled once it is sealed. It uses two פסוקים from ירמיהו that seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק says washing your heart through תשובה works, and the other says no amount of washing removes the stain. The גמרא suggests the natural way to settle this: one is before the גזר דין and one is after. If that is right, then after the decree תשובה cannot help, even for a ציבור.

keyTerms.meaning: The final sealed decree or sentence from Heaven
A community, as opposed to a single person
Isn't it that, introducing a suggested reading

steps.confusionAlert: The 'מאי לאו' reading (before versus after the decree) is only a suggestion that the גמרא is about to reject. Do not treat it as the final answer.

phrases.english: And can a decree on a community really be torn up?
But one verse says:
"Wash your heart from wickedness,"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 4:14

phrases.english: and it is written: "For though you wash with lye
and use much soap,
your sin remains a stain before Me."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 2:22

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו: כָּאן קוֹדֶם גְּזַר דִּין,
phrases.english: Isn't it that here it is before the decree,
and there it is after the decree!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּגְזַר דִּין דְּצִבּוּר מִי מִיקְּרַע? וְהָא כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ציבור and challenges step 2's claim that a community's גזר דין can be torn up even after it is issued.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (step 2) that a community's גזר דין can be torn up through תשובה even after it is issued.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both פסוקים in ירמיהו are addressed to the whole people. The obvious way to settle them is before versus after the decree, which would mean that even a community's תשובה does not help after the decree.

steps.title: Decrees with an oath versus decrees without an oath
steps.stepSummary: Both פסוקים are about after the decree. The difference is whether the decree was sealed with a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Both פסוקים are talking about after the decree, and there is no contradiction. One is about a decree that has an oath with it, which cannot be undone. The other is about a decree without an oath, which can still be undone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the before/after reading. It explains that both פסוקים deal with a sealed decree, but one decree came with an oath from ה׳ and the other did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is that being after the גזר דין is not what blocks תשובה. A decree that ה׳ sealed with a שבועה cannot be torn up. A decree without one can still be canceled, even after it is issued, so the rule that a ציבור can be forgiven after the sentence still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both cases
An oath; here, an oath of ה׳ not to cancel the decree
And it is not difficult; there is no contradiction

steps.whatToRemember: After a גזר דין, תשובה can still tear it up unless the decree was sealed with a שבועה.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי לְאַחַר גְּזַר דִּין,
phrases.english: No, both this one and that one are after the decree,
and it is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּגְזַר דִּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמּוֹ שְׁבוּעָה,
phrases.english: here it is a decree that has an oath with it,

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּגְזַר דִּין שֶׁאֵין עִמּוֹ שְׁבוּעָה.
phrases.english: and there it is a decree that has no oath with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי לְאַחַר גְּזַר דִּין, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by offering a different way to split the two פסוקים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases (oath versus no oath) instead of timing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים differ by timing: before versus after the decree.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are after the decree. Only a decree sealed with a שבועה cannot be torn up.

steps.title: Proof from the oath against the house of Eli
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר אמי (or רב שמואל בר נחמני) in the name of רב יונתן brings a פסוק showing that a decree with an oath cannot be undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רב שמואל בר אמי. Some say it was רב שמואל בר נחמני, quoting רב יונתן: How do we know that a decree with an oath is not torn up? Because the פסוק says, 'And therefore I have sworn to the house of עלי that the sin of the house of עלי will not be atoned with sacrifice or offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for the idea it just used: a decree sealed with an oath stays in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ swore that בית עלי's sin would not be atoned. Since the decree came with a שבועה, it cannot simply be torn up. This backs up the oath / no-oath split from the previous step.

keyTerms.meaning: The family of עלי the כהן גדול

phrases.english: This is like רב שמואל בר אמי,
as רב שמואל בר אמי said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ, אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
phrases.english: and some say it was רב שמואל בר נחמני who said,
רב יונתן said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִגְזַר דִּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמּוֹ שְׁבוּעָה
phrases.english: From where do we know that a decree that has an oath with it
is not torn up?
As it says: "And therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording, to match the פסוק.

phrases.english: that the sin of Eli's house will not be atoned
with sacrifice or offering."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 3:14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the oath / no-oath split used in the answer.
steps.raayaObject: A decree sealed with a שבועה is not torn up.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 3:14, ה׳'s oath to בית עלי.

steps.title: רבא: Torah can still atone for the house of Eli
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the פסוק narrowly: only sacrifices cannot atone. תורה can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Through sacrifice and offering it is not atoned, but it can be atoned through תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא looks closely at the wording of the oath and finds an opening. The oath only says sacrifices will not help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names only זבח and מנחה. רבא takes this to mean the oath blocks only those paths, so learning תורה can still bring כפרה, even for a sworn decree.

phrases.english: Rava said:
With sacrifice and offering it is not atoned,
but it is atoned through Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּזֶבַח וּבַמִּנְחָה אֵינוֹ מִתְכַּפֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the פסוק of בית עלי by reading its limits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The oath blocks only קרבנות; תורה still brings כפרה.

steps.title: אביי: Torah and kindness both atone
steps.stepSummary: אביי agrees with רבא and adds that גמילות חסדים also atones.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Through sacrifice and offering it is not atoned, but it is atoned through תורה and acts of kindness.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the same reading as רבא but widens it. Both תורה and גמילות חסדים can atone for בית עלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבא, אביי says the oath blocks only קרבנות. He adds a second path, גמילות חסדים, so the opening is wider.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing acts of kindness for others

phrases.english: Abaye said:
With sacrifice and offering it is not atoned,
but it is atoned through Torah and acts of kindness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: בְּזֶבַח וּמִנְחָה אֵינוֹ מִתְכַּפֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a broader version of רבא's reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תורה and גמילות חסדים both bring כפרה, even for a sworn decree.

steps.title: רבה and אביי from the house of Eli
steps.stepSummary: A story: רבה, who learned תורה, lived forty years. אביי, who learned תורה and did kindness, lived sixty years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and אביי both came from the family of עלי. רבה, who was busy with תורה, lived forty years. אביי, who was busy with תורה and acts of kindness, lived sixty years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that shows the two opinions in action. Both men came from the family under the curse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each man lived by his own view. רבה's תורה gained him some years, and אביי's תורה together with kindness gained him even more. This supports the idea that the sworn decree on בית עלי can be softened, and that adding kindness helps further.

keyTerms.meaning: Was busy with, devoted himself to

steps.whatToRemember: Even a decree sealed with a שבועה can be softened by תורה, and even more by תורה together with גמילות חסדים, as the lives of רבה and אביי show.

phrases.english: Rabba and Abaye came from the house of Eli.
Rabba, who was busy with Torah,
lived forty years;
Abaye, who was busy with Torah and acts of kindness,
lived sixty years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the two readings of רבא and אביי through their own lives.
steps.raayaObject: תורה, and even more תורה with גמילות חסדים, can soften the sworn decree on בית עלי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The lifespans of רבה (forty years) and אביי (sixty years).

steps.title: A family in ירושלים is saved by learning תורה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a family in ירושלים whose members died at eighteen. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי guessed they came from עלי, told them to learn תורה, and they lived.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: a family in ירושלים kept dying at age eighteen. They told רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. He said: maybe you come from עלי's family, whose men were cursed to die young. Go learn תורה and you will live. They did, and they lived, and people named the family after רבן יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that backs up רבא's teaching that תורה can save עלי's descendants from their curse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said sacrifices cannot fix the decree on עלי's house, but תורה can. Here we see it happen: the curse of dying young was real, and learning תורה broke it.

keyTerms.meaning: The family of עלי the כהן, whose descendants were cursed to die young
The growth of your household, meaning your descendants

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבא's reading is not just theory. The power of תורה to change a sealed decree is shown in real life.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There was one family in Jerusalem

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיוּ מֵתֶיהָ מֵתִין בְּנֵי שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה.
phrases.english: whose members would die at eighteen years old.

phrases.aramaic: בָּאוּ וְהוֹדִיעוּ אֶת רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי,
phrases.english: They came and told Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: שֶׁמָּא מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת עֵלִי אַתֶּם,
phrases.english: He said to them: Perhaps you are from the family of Eli,
about whom it is written:
"And all the increase of your house shall die as young men."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 2:33

phrases.english: Go and busy yourselves with Torah, and live.
They went and busied themselves with Torah, and they lived.
And people would call it
the family of Rabban Yochanan, after his name.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִשְׁפָּחָה אַחַת הָיְתָה בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story supporting the idea that Torah atones for עלי's house, after the story of רבה and אביי.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that Torah can undo the decree on עלי's house
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a Jerusalem family saved by רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's advice

steps.title: A community's decree is not sealed
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר אינייא in the name of רב asks for a source that a decree on a community is never sealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר אינייא said in the name of רב: From where do we know that a decree against a community is not sealed?
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins: a decree on a whole community is never sealed. The גמרא is setting up a challenge to this wording, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the stories about the family of עלי, the focus returns to the צבור, the community. The claim is very strong: such a decree is never final.

keyTerms.meaning: A sentence or decree from Heaven

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִינְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Inya said in the name of Rav:
From where do we know that a decree on a community
is not sealed?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִינְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב: מִנַּיִין לִגְזַר דִּין שֶׁל צִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story about the family of עלי, returns to decrees on a community (the topic of steps 10-11) with a new teaching from רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A decree against a community is not sealed.

steps.title: But a פסוק says the community's sin is sealed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim: a פסוק in ירמיהו says the people's sin is 'sealed' before God.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not sealed?! But it is written: 'Your sin is sealed before Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording 'not sealed' using a פסוק spoken to the whole people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירמיהו speaks to all of Israel and says 'נכתם עונך', which the גמרא reads as 'your sin is sealed'. So a community's decree can be sealed, which contradicts the statement.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it not written? Introduces a challenge from a פסוק
Stained or marked; read here as sealed

phrases.english: Not sealed?!
But it is written: "Your sin is sealed before Me"!
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 2:22. The word נכתם sounds like נחתם, sealed, so the גמרא reads it that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a community's decree is never sealed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק addressed to the whole nation says its sin is sealed, so a community decree can be sealed.

steps.title: Even when sealed, it can be torn up
steps.stepSummary: The statement is reworded: a community's decree can be sealed, but it can still be torn up, since God answers whenever we call Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, even though it is sealed, it can be torn up, as it says: 'Like ה׳ our God, whenever we call to Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of רב's teaching so it fits the פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new version agrees that a community's decree can be sealed. What is special is that it can still be torn up. The proof is that God is near to the people 'whenever' they call.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a community's decree never gets sealed. It agrees it can be sealed. The point is that it can still be cancelled afterward.

phrases.english: Rather: even though it is sealed
it can be torn up,
as it says:
"Like ה׳ our God, whenever we call to Him."
phrases.notes: דברים 4:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 by rewording Step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A community's decree is never sealed at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: A community's decree can be sealed, but prayer can still tear it up.

steps.title: But God is found only at certain times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a פסוק in ישעיהו says to seek God 'when He can be found', which suggests He is not always near.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'Seek ה׳ when He can be found.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets one פסוק against another: one says God answers whenever we call, the other says only at certain times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If God answers 'whenever we call', why tell us to seek Him 'when He can be found'? That wording implies there are times He cannot be found.

phrases.english: But it is written: "Seek ה׳ when He can be found"!
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 55:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof פסוק of Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from 'בכל קראנו אליו' that God is always near
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק limits finding God to certain times.

steps.title: One פסוק is about an individual, the other about a community
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the limit in ישעיהו is for an individual; the 'whenever' in דברים is for a community.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is talking about an individual; here it is talking about a community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the two פסוקים by saying they talk about different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual can reach God only at special times. A community can reach God at any time, which is why its sealed decree can still be torn up.
steps.whatToRemember: A community's prayer works at any time, even after a decree is sealed. An individual has special times when God is close.

phrases.english: There, it is about an individual;
phrases.notes: "There" is the פסוק in ישעיהו, "seek ה׳ when He can be found."

phrases.english: here, it is about a community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים describe the same people, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limited time is for an individual; the unlimited access is for a community.

steps.title: When can an individual find God?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if an individual can find God only at certain times, when are those times?
steps.simpleTranslation: For an individual, when is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question to the last answer, setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned an individual can reach God only 'when He can be found'. Now we want to know which time that is.

phrases.english: For an individual, when?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the individual case from Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The time when God is near to an individual

steps.title: The ten days from ראש השנה to יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה answers: the time is the ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר אבוה said: These are the ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר אבוה answers the question: an individual can find God during the ten days from ראש השנה to יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives a fixed time to 'when He can be found'. During these days an individual's prayer and תשובה work in a special way.

keyTerms.meaning: The new year, the day of judgment

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a main source for the special status of the עשרת ימי תשובה.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Avuh said:
These are the ten days
between Rosh HaShanah and Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: אֵלּוּ עֲשָׂרָה יָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים

steps.title: Why did נבל die ten days later?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק that God struck נבל about ten days later and asks what those ten days were for.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And about ten days later ה׳ struck נבל.' What were these ten days for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the פסוק mentions a ten-day delay before נבל was punished. The answers come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבל insulted דוד and deserved punishment right away. The פסוק stresses a wait of ten days, so the גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: What is their purpose? What are they doing here?

phrases.english: "And it was about ten days later,
and ה׳ struck Naval."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 25:38

phrases.english: These ten days, what were they for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings up another 'ten days' in תנ"ך, to be compared with the ten days just mentioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the ten-day delay before נבל's death

steps.title: Ten days for the ten portions נבל gave דוד's servants
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב says the ten days match the ten portions of food נבל gave to דוד's servants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: They match the ten portions of food that נבל gave to דוד's servants.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: נבל got ten extra days as a reward for the small kindness of feeding דוד's servants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a wicked person gets paid for good deeds. Each portion of food bought נבל one more day of life.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
They match the ten portions of food
that Naval gave to David's servants.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: כְּנֶגֶד עֶשֶׂר לְגִימוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten days were a reward for ten portions of food נבל gave.

steps.title: נבל's ten days were the days of תשובה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה says the ten days were the ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: These are the ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer: נבל's ten days were the ten days of תשובה, a last chance to repent before his punishment came.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same words as רבה בר אבוה's earlier answer, now applied to נבל. So נבל was judged on ראש השנה, given until יום הכפורים to repent, and died when he did not. This also supports the idea that these days are a special time for an individual.

keyTerms.meaning: The rich man who insulted דוד (שמואל א 25)

steps.whatToRemember: An individual can reach God at special times, the ten days from ראש השנה to יום הכפורים. Even נבל got these ten days to repent before being punished.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
These are the ten days
phrases.notes: Same words as in Step 23, but now they explain נבל's ten days.

phrases.english: between Rosh HaShanah and Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: אֵלּוּ עֲשָׂרָה יָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer from Step 25 to the question in Step 24, using רבה בר אבוה's idea from Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten days were the days of תשובה between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים, given to נבל to repent.

steps.title: The גמרא returns to the phrase 'like בני מרון'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה that on ראש השנה everyone passes before God like בני מרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ראש השנה, every person in the world passes before God like 'בני מרון'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line from the משנה so it can explain an unclear phrase in it. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said everyone is judged on ראש השנה, but used an unusual phrase, 'כבני מרון', to describe how they pass before God. The גמרא now focuses on that phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone who comes into the world, meaning all people
Pass before Him, to be judged
An unclear phrase describing how people pass before God; the גמרא will explain it

phrases.english: On Rosh HaShanah, all who come into the world
pass before Him like benei maron.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כׇּל בָּאֵי הָעוֹלָם עוֹבְרִין לְפָנָיו כִּבְנֵי מָרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the discussion of the ten days of repentance to explain another phrase in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone is judged on ראש השנה, passing before God 'כבני מרון'

steps.title: What does 'like בני מרון' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the phrase כבני מרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'like בני מרון' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the strange phrase 'כבני מרון' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple word question, not a challenge. The answers that follow will each give a different picture of how people pass before God.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What is "like benei maron"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the phrase just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase כבני מרון

steps.title: First explanation: like a flock of sheep
steps.stepSummary: In בבל they explained כבני מרון as 'like a flock of sheep'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here in בבל they translated it as: like a flock of sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: the phrase means 'like sheep', which pass one at a time before the shepherd.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The picture is a shepherd counting his sheep as they pass one by one. So each person on ראש השנה is checked individually by God.

phrases.english: Here they translated it: like a flock of sheep.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means in בבל, where this גמרא was learned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כבני מרון means like a flock of sheep

steps.title: Second explanation: like the path up בית מרון
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains it as like the steep ascent of בית מרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: it means like the steps going up to בית מרון.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different answer: the phrase refers to a steep, narrow path at a place called בית מרון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a narrow path people must walk one behind the other, and someone at the top can see each of them. Like the first answer, it shows each person passing alone, but with a different picture.

keyTerms.meaning: A place with a steep, narrow climb

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: כְּמַעֲלוֹת בֵּית מָרוֹן.
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: like the ascents of Beit Maron.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation of the same phrase
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Like people climbing the narrow path of בית מרון

steps.title: Third explanation: like the soldiers of בית דוד
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains it as like the soldiers of the house of דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: it means like the soldiers of בית דוד.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a third answer: the phrase means like an army of soldiers of דוד המלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An army passes before its king in review, and he inspects them. So too all people pass before God the King to be judged.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Like the soldiers of the house of David.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third explanation of the same phrase
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Like soldiers of בית דוד passing in review

steps.title: Everyone is seen in one single look
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds that even though people pass one by one, God sees all of them in one look.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: and they are all looked over in one single look.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds an important point: God does not need a long time to judge everyone; He sees them all at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three pictures might suggest God checks people one after another. רבי יוחנן says that although each person is judged individually, God takes them all in with one glance.
steps.confusionAlert: Being judged 'one by one' and being seen 'in one look' are not a contradiction: each person gets individual attention, but God does it all at once.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
And they are all looked over in a single look.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a point to the pictures of people passing before God
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God sees and judges all people in one single look

steps.title: A proof from a פסוק in תהלים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings the פסוק 'היוצר יחד לבם' as support for רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: we also learned this in our משנה, which quotes the פסוק: 'He Who forms their hearts together, Who understands all their deeds.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק says there is a פסוק that supports רבי יוחנן's idea. The גמרא will next work out how the פסוק proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is 'יחד' (together). The proof only works once we understand what 'together' refers to, which the next steps explain.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (from a source)
The One Who forms, the Creator

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
We too have also learned this:
phrases.notes: He means our own משנה, which ends this line with this very פסוק.

phrases.english: "He Who forms their hearts together,
phrases.notes: תהלים 33:15

phrases.english: Who understands all their deeds."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק to support רבי יוחנן
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's statement that all are seen in one look
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 33:15, היוצר יחד לבם המבין אל כל מעשיהם

steps.title: What is the פסוק saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the פסוק means, to see how it proves the point.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the פסוק really means. This sets up a wrong reading and then the correct one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on how we read 'יחד לבם'. The גמרא will test one possible reading before reaching the right one.

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the פסוק just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The correct reading of 'היוצר יחד לבם'

steps.title: It cannot mean God makes all hearts the same
steps.stepSummary: Reading the פסוק as 'God makes everyone's hearts alike' is rejected, because we see people are not alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means: He created everyone and makes their hearts the same as each other, but we see that this is not so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one way of reading the פסוק and throws it out, because it does not match reality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'יחד לבם' meant God makes all hearts identical, the פסוק would be false, since people obviously think and feel differently. So 'together' must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a reading about to be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say this is what it is saying:
That He created everyone
and makes their hearts one, like each other —

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא קָא חָזֵינַן דְּלָאו הָכִי הוּא!
phrases.english: but we see that it is not so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects a first possible reading of the פסוק
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that God makes all hearts identical
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It contradicts what we see, since people's hearts are different

steps.title: The פסוק means God sees all hearts together
steps.stepSummary: The correct reading: the Creator sees all their hearts together and understands all their deeds, proving רבי יוחנן's point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must mean this: the Creator sees their hearts together, and understands all their deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reading of the פסוק, and with it the proof is complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יחד' describes God's seeing, not the hearts themselves: He looks at everyone's heart at the same time. That is exactly רבי יוחנן's idea that all are seen in one look.
steps.whatToRemember: On ראש השנה each person passes before God individually (sheep, a narrow path, or soldiers), yet God sees all of them together in one look, as the פסוק 'היוצר יחד לבם' teaches.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that this is what it is saying:
The Creator sees their hearts together,
phrases.notes: The גמרא adds the word 'sees' to the פסוק, so 'together' describes how God looks, not how the hearts are.

phrases.english: and understands all their deeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading with the correct one
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק teaches that God sees all hearts together, supporting רבי יוחנן

steps.title: The משנה: six months when messengers go out
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists six months when the בית דין sends messengers to announce the day of ראש חודש, and the holiday each one is for.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: In six months the messengers go out: in ניסן because of פסח, in אב because of the fast, in אלול because of ראש השנה, in תשרי to set the holidays correctly, in כסלו because of חנוכה, and in אדר because of פורים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the months when the בית דין sent messengers to tell people which day was ראש חודש, so they would keep that month's holiday on the right day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Messengers were only sent in months that have a holiday whose date depends on knowing when the month began. Each month is paired with its reason: פסח, תשעה באב, ראש השנה, the holidays of תשרי, חנוכה, and פורים.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (start of a new משנה)
Messengers sent by the בית דין

phrases.english: MISHNA: In six months
the messengers go out:
in Nisan, because of Pesach;
in Av, because of the fast;
in Elul, because of Rosh HaShanah;
in Tishrei, to set the festivals correctly;
in Kislev, because of Chanukah;
and in Adar, because of Purim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Messengers go out in ניסן, אב, אלול, תשרי, כסלו, and אדר to announce ראש חודש for each month's holiday

steps.title: During the בית המקדש: also in אייר for פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: When the בית המקדש stood, messengers also went out in אייר because of פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when the בית המקדש was standing, they also went out in אייר, because of the 'small פסח'.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a seventh month that applied only while the בית המקדש stood: אייר, for פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח שני is a second chance to bring the קרבן פסח, which only matters when there is a בית המקדש. So once it was destroyed, there was no longer a reason to send messengers in אייר.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'small פסח', meaning פסח שני on 14 אייר

steps.whatToRemember: Messengers go out in six months, each tied to a holiday; while the בית המקדש stood, a seventh month, אייר, was added for פסח שני.

phrases.english: And when the Temple was standing —
they would go out also in Iyyar
because of the small Pesach.
phrases.notes: This is פסח שני, a month after פסח, for people who could not bring the קרבן פסח in time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a seventh month to the list, only for the time of the בית המקדש
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While the בית המקדש stood, messengers also went out in אייר for פסח שני

steps.title: Why not send messengers for תמוז and טבת too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's list: if messengers go out in אב for its fast, they should also go out in תמוז and טבת, which have fasts too.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Let the messengers also go out for the months of תמוז and טבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a challenge. If messengers are sent in אב so people know when the fast day falls, why not also in תמוז and טבת, which also have fast days?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's reason for אב is a fast day, תשעה באב. But תמוז has the fast of שבעה עשר בתמוז and טבת has the fast of עשרה בטבת. So by the משנה's own logic, the list of six months looks incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: And let them go out (the messengers)
The month of תמוז, which has the fast of the 17th
The month of טבת, which has the fast of the 10th

steps.confusionAlert: The fasts are not written in the text here. The גמרא assumes you know that תמוז and טבת each have a public fast, like אב does.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And let them also go out
for Tammuz and Tevet!
phrases.notes: These months have fast days too: the 17th of תמוז and the 10th of טבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's list of months (Step 37), challenging it as incomplete.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's list of six months when messengers go out, which includes אב because of the fast but leaves out תמוז and טבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a fast day is enough reason to send messengers in אב, the same reason should apply to תמוז and טבת, which also have public fasts.
